text:
ashley: Heads up 1 I installed redwoodctl via snap on Ubuntu 22.04 and hit an auth redirect mismatch when running `redwoodctl local-serve`. Browser opens, callback returns code, CLI says `oauth: redirect_uri mismatch`. Anyone familiar with snap quirks here?

liam: Snap confinement can change runtime behavior (env vars, network namespace). Did you use `snap install redwoodctl --classic` or the confined snap?

ashley: default snap from our PPA mirror (non-classic). Repro steps:
1) `snap install redwoodctl`
2) `redwoodctl login --profile dev` (works, browser open)
3) `redwoodctl local-serve --profile dev` -> browser opens to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/callback?code=...` then CLI prints `oauth: redirect_uri mismatch` and exits.

sam: Do you see any logs from the CLI about the callback it registered? Could be binding to `127.0.1.1` or `localhost` while the callback URL uses a different host. Snap may affect /etc/hosts resolution (Ubuntu sets hostname -> 127.0.1.1).

ashley: Yeah I inspected `~/.config/redwood/local-serve.json` and the `redirect_uri` the CLI generated was `http://hostname:8080/callback` (hostname maps to 127.0.1.1), but browser used 127.0.0.1. So OAuth provider rejected it.

kevin: Hmm, we used to generate redirect URIs from the system hostname if localhost was ambiguous. That's fragile in containerized/snap envs. We should prefer `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` or normalize both sides to `localhost` for the auth state.

jen: For docs: call out that confined snaps may change hostname resolution and recommend `--classic` or manual install until fixed. Also include the `/snap/.../current/bin/redwoodctl` path workaround.

ashley: Workaround that worked for me: `snap run --shell redwoodctl` then run the bundled binary directly: `/snap/redwoodctl/current/bin/redwoodctl local-serve --profile dev`. That avoids the wrapper and uses 127.0.0.1 consistently.

sam: Good short-term fix. Longer term: add a CLI patch to always bind to 127.0.0.1 and write redirect URI with numeric host, and also accept callbacks to the hostname variant (tolerate 127.0.1.1 and localhost). Might also add a heuristic: if hostname resolves to 127.* prefer numeric form.

kevin: I'll take this. Plan: PR to normalize callback host -> prefer 127.0.0.1, add unit test that simulates hostname->127.0.1.1 mapping, and add a line to install docs warning about confined snaps.

devex-bot: Issue created: #4621 "snap install: auth redirect mismatch in confined snaps" assigned to @kevin and @sam. ETA: next sprint.

sam: I'll add the network-namespace integration test to CI so we catch regressions.

liam: Also consider adding a CLI flag `--redirect-host` for advanced users to explicitly set the callback host during dev. Could be useful for corporate VPNs.

ashley: Thanks all 60; workaround and notes saved in my onboarding doc. Putting a note in #snapcraft channel too in case folks report similar.
